app.title: Cell Surveillance — single-cell tracking
app.summary: A person loads a time-lapse movie by dropping it, browsing for it or pasting its path, and previews a frame with the detected nuclei outlined. They enter the time between frames and confirm a scale (the scale bar found in the movie, or the pixel size). They pick which measurements to run, then start the analysis. Every nucleus is tracked, and the tool calls nuclear ruptures, divisions and deaths cell by cell. They read the totals and plots, adjust what counts as a rupture without tracking again, open single cells to check their image strips and traces, and export tables, an annotated movie and a PDF report, either for the whole field or for a region they draw.

task.text: Track every cell in a live-cell movie, find nuclear rupture, division and death events for each cell, and export per-cell and population measurements.

data.text: A time-lapse fluorescence movie of a nuclear reporter. It is turned into per-cell tracks, one row per cell per frame with position, intensity and shape, plus tables of detected events and population time courses.
data.item: a tracked cell: one nucleus followed across the frames of a time-lapse movie

stage.text: quantifying cell events from raw time-lapse movies after imaging, before writing up

mechanism.text: Setup is a four-step panel (movie, calibrate, measure, run) with a frame preview. The Run button stays disabled until the calibration is complete. Once the analysis has run, a menu opens result views: an overview dashboard, a rupture view where a threshold slider and a sweep curve re-call events without re-tracking, movement and fate charts, a sortable cell table that opens one cell's image strip and traces, a region view where a box dragged on the frame selects cells for export, and an export page.

field.text: single-cell tracking and event detection in live-cell fluorescence imaging in cell biology

workflow.name: track objects through a movie, call events per object, and export per-object measurements

steps.here: Drop a MOV/MP4/AVI/TIFF movie, choose one with the native file dialog or paste a path. A frame slider previews the movie with the detected nuclei outlined. Earlier analyses can be reopened from History.

steps.step: enter the calibration and choose what to measure
steps.here: Enter the minutes between frames. For scale, tick to confirm the auto-detected scale bar and give its length, or enter µm per pixel. Tick rupture, movement, division, death, shape or crowding, and set the rupture mode and threshold. 'Analyse movie' stays disabled until everything is entered.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Analysing the movie runs segmentation, tracking and event calling in a subprocess, with a progress bar. It then opens the results.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The overview shows tiles for cells tracked, ruptures, divisions, deaths and speed, next to the looping annotated movie, cumulative-event curves and the fraction of cells ruptured over time.

Change the rupture mode or threshold with a slider shown against a sweep of how many ruptures each threshold gives. 'Apply' re-calls the events without tracking again. Image strips of the largest, smallest or longest ruptures help check the calls. A wrong calibration can be corrected the same way.

Sort the cell table by ruptures, time observed, path length or speed, and pick a row. That cell's image strip, reporter trace with ruptures shaded, speed trace and every measurement appear beside the table.

Drag a box on the frame, or type its coordinates, and choose a rule for which cells count as inside, then export the cropped movie, tables and report for that region. The export page has download buttons for each file, a zip of all tables, and buttons to rebuild the movie or the report.

distinctive: The frame interval and the scale are never assumed. Each must be entered for every movie before the analysis can run, and a detected scale bar is shown outlined for the person to confirm.
The event threshold can be changed after tracking. A sweep curve shows how many ruptures each threshold would call, and applying it re-calls events without tracking again.
Finished results can be recalibrated: every time, speed, distance and area is recomputed, and a warning stays up until the calibration is confirmed.
Each track ends in a fate (divided, death, left the field, hidden by a neighbour, lost), and death calls carry a confidence level and the evidence behind them.
A region can be exported with a rule for which cells belong to it (inside most of the time, at any time, at the start, or always).
